routes.label: Compare the station positions as fractions of total race length

question:
Along the route of a bicycle race, \(7\) water stations are evenly spaced between the start and finish lines, as shown in the figure below. There are also \(2\) repair stations evenly spaced between the start and finish lines. The \(3\)rd water station is located \(2\) miles after the \(1\)st repair station. How long is the race in miles?

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_8_Q13_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Count the gaps, including those next to the start and finish. Seven water stations divide the race into \(8\) equal gaps, while two repair stations divide it into \(3\) equal gaps.

The third water station is therefore \(\frac38\) of the way along the course, and the first repair station is \(\frac13\) of the way along. The distance between them is this fraction of the race:

\[
\frac38-\frac13=\frac9{24}-\frac8{24}=\frac1{24}.
\]

That fraction is \(2\) miles, so the whole race is

\[
24\cdot2=\boxed{48}\text{ miles},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\). With evenly spaced interior stations, the number of equal gaps is one more than the number of stations.
